intent: Initialize NestJS project with Postgres database and configuration
instructions: Create NestJS project structure: nest new timesheet-backend (or scaffold from scratch). Install: @nestjs/common, @nestjs/core, @nestjs/platform-express, @nestjs/typeorm, @nestjs/jwt, @nestjs/passport, typeorm, pg, bcrypt, class-validator, class-transformer, passport-jwt. Create .env file with: DB_URI (postgres://localhost:5432/timesheet), JWT_SECRET, NODE_ENV. Configure TypeOrmModule with synchronize: true for development. Test: npm run start should start dev server on port 3001.
acceptance_criteria: npm run start starts server on port 3001

intent: Configure TypeORM and PostgreSQL connection
instructions: Create TypeORM configuration (ormconfig.ts or dataSource.ts) with PostgreSQL connection. Configure: host (localhost), port (5432), username, password, database (timesheet), synchronize (true for dev), logging (true for dev). Create database.module.ts exporting TypeOrmModule.forRoot(). Test: npm run typeorm:migration:generate -- creates migration files without error.

intent: Create User entity with email, password_hash, role, status
instructions: Create src/modules/user/user.entity.ts with columns: id (UUID primary), email (unique varchar), password_hash (varchar), role (enum: ADMIN, MANAGER, USER), status (enum: active, inactive), created_at (timestamp), updated_at (timestamp). Add indexes on email. Create migration. Test: npm run typeorm:migration:run generates user table with constraints.
acceptance_criteria: User entity defined with all fields
Email unique constraint at DB level

intent: Create password hashing and verification service
instructions: Create src/modules/auth/password.service.ts with methods: hashPassword(plaintext): Promise<string> using bcrypt rounds=10, verifyPassword(plaintext, hash): Promise<boolean>. Add password strength validator: min 8 chars, 1 uppercase, 1 digit. Test: inject service, test hash('Test123!') produces $2 hash, verify('Test123!', hash) returns true, verify('wrong', hash) returns false.
acceptance_criteria: Password hashing uses bcrypt with salt rounds 10

intent: Configure JWT authentication strategy with Passport
instructions: Create src/modules/auth/jwt.strategy.ts extending PassportStrategy(Strategy, 'jwt'). Configure: secret from env, extract from 'Authorization' header (Bearer format), return user object with id, email, role. Create jwt-auth.guard.ts applying this strategy. Test: send request with valid JWT in header, verify passed. Send without token, verify 401.
acceptance_criteria: JWT strategy configured with secret from env
Bearer token extracted from Authorization header
User object attached to request with id, email, role

intent: Create POST /auth/signup endpoint with validation and user creation
instructions: Create src/modules/auth/auth.controller.ts with POST /signup. Accept {email: string, password: string, name?: string}. Validate email format, password strength. Check duplicate email. Hash password using PasswordService. Create user in DB with role=USER. Return {access_token: string, user: {id, email, name, role}} (exclude password_hash). Test: curl -X POST http://localhost:3001/auth/signup -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"test@example.com","password":"Test123!"}', verify 201 and JWT returned. Test duplicate email returns 409.

intent: Create POST /auth/login endpoint with credentials verification
instructions: Create POST /login in auth.controller.ts. Accept {email, password}. Find user by email. Verify password using PasswordService. Return {access_token, user} or 401. Test: curl with valid credentials (test@example.com/Test123!), verify 200 and JWT. Test with wrong password, verify 401 with message 'Invalid credentials'.
acceptance_criteria: Does not leak user existence (same error for missing/wrong password)

intent: Create role-based access control (RBAC) guard
instructions: Create src/modules/auth/roles.guard.ts with @RequireRole() decorator accepting array of roles. Check user.role from JWT against required roles. Return 403 if not authorized. Apply guard to endpoints. Test: create endpoint requiring MANAGER role, test with USER token (403), MANAGER token (200).
acceptance_criteria: Guard checks user role from JWT
Admin role bypasses all role checks
User gets 403 if role not in required list

intent: Create Project entity with code, description, dates
instructions: Create src/modules/project/project.entity.ts with columns: id (UUID), code (varchar 10, unique), description (varchar 40), default_task (varchar 100), start_date (date), end_date (date), status (enum: active, completed, archived), created_by_id (FK to User), created_at, updated_at. Add check constraint: end_date >= start_date. Create migration. Test: create project, verify all fields stored correctly.
acceptance_criteria: Project entity has all required fields
Code is unique and max 10 chars

intent: Create Project CRUD endpoints (Create, Read, Update, List, Archive)
instructions: Create src/modules/project/project.controller.ts with endpoints: POST /projects (create), GET /projects (list), GET /projects/:id (read), PATCH /projects/:id (update), DELETE /projects/:id (archive). Only creator or ADMIN can edit/delete. List excludes archived by default unless ?include_archived=true. Paginate: limit (default 20), offset (default 0). Test: curl -X POST http://localhost:3001/projects with valid project data, verify 201. GET /projects, verify list excludes archived. Test permission: non-creator tries to PATCH, verify 403.
acceptance_criteria: POST creates project with code unique check
GET lists projects, excludes archived by default
Returns total count for pagination UI

intent: Create Timesheet entity with status, week tracking, total hours
instructions: Create src/modules/timesheet/timesheet.entity.ts with columns: id (UUID), tm_id (varchar, auto-generated TM00001 format, unique), user_id (FK), project_id (FK), status (enum: draft, pending, approved), week_start_date (date, Monday), week_end_date (date, Sunday), total_hours (decimal, read-only/computed), comments (text max 500), rejection_comment (text, nullable), created_at, updated_at. Add check constraint: week_end_date = week_start_date + 6 days. Create migration. Test: create timesheet, verify TM ID auto-generates.
acceptance_criteria: Timesheet entity created with all fields
TM ID auto-generates as TM00001, TM00002, etc

intent: Create TimesheetEntry entity for daily hour tracking
instructions: Create src/modules/timesheet/timesheet-entry.entity.ts with columns: id (UUID), timesheet_id (FK), project_task (varchar, task name), entry_date (date), hours (decimal precision 3,2 for 0-8 range), created_at, updated_at. Add check constraint: hours >= 0 AND hours <= 8. Add index on (timesheet_id, entry_date). Create migration. Test: insert entry with 5.5 hours, verify stored. Try to insert 8.1 hours, verify constraint rejects.
acceptance_criteria: Hours stored as decimal, allow 0.5, 1.25, etc
entry_date must be within timesheet week
Check constraint enforced at DB level

intent: Create TimesheetEntry CRUD with 8hr/day and 40hr/week validation
instructions: Create src/modules/timesheet/timesheet-entry.controller.ts and service. Endpoints: POST /timesheets/:id/entries, GET /timesheets/:id/entries, PATCH /timesheets/:id/entries/:entryId, DELETE /timesheets/:id/entries/:entryId. Validation in service: total_hours_per_day (sum of all entries for that date) <= 8, total_hours_per_week (sum for week) <= 40. User can only edit if timesheet status is draft or pending. Test: POST entry 5 hours, should succeed. POST another 4 same day (total 9), should fail with 'Daily limit exceeded (8 hours max)'. POST entries totaling 40 hours, succeed. POST 41st, fail with 'Weekly limit exceeded (40 hours max)'.
acceptance_criteria: Daily limit (8 hrs) enforced with clear message
Weekly limit (40 hrs) enforced with clear message
User can only edit own timesheet

intent: Create GET /timesheets with filtering, pagination, role-based access
instructions: Create GET /timesheets endpoint in timesheet.controller.ts. User: only own timesheets. Admin: all timesheets. Manager: own + team. Filters: user_id (required for non-admin), project_id, status, week_start_date (range). Paginate: limit (default 20), offset. Response: array of timesheets with week_start, week_end, status, total_hours. Test: curl GET /timesheets (own), GET /timesheets?status=pending, GET /timesheets?week_start_date=2025-01-20&week_end_date=2025-01-26.

intent: Create PATCH /timesheets/:id/submit endpoint (draft to pending)
instructions: Create PATCH /timesheets/:id/submit endpoint. Validates: timesheet is draft, has at least 1 entry, all entries valid. Transitions status from draft to pending. User can only submit own timesheet. Once submitted, entries cannot be edited (except by manager reject). Test: user creates entries, submits (status changes to pending), tries to POST new entry, gets 400 'Cannot edit pending timesheet'.

intent: Create PATCH /timesheets/:id/approve and /reject endpoints
instructions: Create PATCH /timesheets/:id/approve (MANAGER only): transitions pending->approved, read-only after. Create PATCH /timesheets/:id/reject (MANAGER only): requires {rejection_comment} body, stores comment, transitions to draft (editable again). Test: manager approves pending timesheet, verify status approved. Try to edit, get 400 'Cannot edit approved'. Manager rejects, timesheet back to draft with comment visible.
acceptance_criteria: Reject stores comment, sets status to draft

intent: Implement total_hours calculation as computed property
instructions: Add method in Timesheet entity or service: calculateTotalHours() sums all TimesheetEntry.hours for that timesheet. Expose as read-only property/method. When fetching timesheet, always calculate fresh. Test: create timesheet, add entries (5, 3, 2 hours = 10 total), fetch, verify total_hours = 10.

intent: Create GET /reports/hours endpoint for aggregated hours by date range
instructions: Create src/modules/report/report.controller.ts with GET /reports/hours?user_id=&date_from=&date_to=. Returns {user: {id, email, name}, date_range: {from, to}, total_hours: number, by_week: [{week_start, week_end, hours}], by_project: [{project_id, project_name, hours}]}. Only approved timesheets count. User can see own, admin sees all, manager sees team. Test: curl GET /reports/hours?user_id=uuid&date_from=2025-01-01&date_to=2025-01-31, verify totals match manual calculation.

intent: Create GET /reports/hours/export?format=csv endpoint
instructions: Extend report endpoint to support format=csv query param. Returns CSV with headers: User,Project,Task,StartDate,EndDate,Hours,Status,WeekTotal. One row per timesheet entry. Include weekly subtotal rows. Response headers: Content-Type: text/csv, Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=report-YYYYMMDD.csv. Test: curl 'http://localhost:3001/reports/hours/export?user_id=uuid&format=csv' -o report.csv, verify CSV format (proper escaping, quotes for strings).

intent: Implement global error handling and logging
instructions: Create src/common/filters/http-exception.filter.ts for exception handling. Catch all exceptions, return standardized error response: {statusCode, message, timestamp, path, error: {details}}. Log errors with context (user, endpoint, stack). Test: trigger 404, verify formatted response. Trigger 400 validation, verify message. Check logs contain context.
acceptance_criteria: Exception filter catches all HTTP exceptions

intent: Add DTO validation using class-validator and ValidationPipe
instructions: Create DTOs: src/modules/auth/dto/signup.dto.ts {email: string, password: string}, login.dto.ts, create-project.dto.ts, create-timesheet-entry.dto.ts. Use @IsEmail(), @MinLength(), @IsDate() decorators. Apply global ValidationPipe in main.ts. Test: send invalid email to signup, verify 400 'Email must be valid'. Send password < 8 chars, verify error.

intent: Implement structured logging for debugging and monitoring
instructions: Create src/common/logger/logger.service.ts with methods: log(), error(), warn(), debug(). Inject into services. Log: incoming requests (method, path, user), database operations (slow queries), errors with full context. Use console.log or Winston library. Test: check logs when signup/login/create entry executed.

intent: Configure CORS for frontend communication
instructions: In main.ts, enable CORS with: origins (http://localhost:3000, http://localhost:5173), credentials: true, methods: GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE. Test: frontend can call backend endpoints from different port.
acceptance_criteria: Frontend can call API without CORS error

intent: Create /health and /health/db endpoints for monitoring
instructions: Create src/modules/health/health.controller.ts with GET /health returning {status: 'ok', timestamp}. GET /health/db returns {status: 'ok'/'error', database: 'connected'/'disconnected'}. Test: curl http://localhost:3001/health, verify 200 {status: ok}. Curl /health/db, verify database status.

intent: Create database seed script for testing
instructions: Create src/database/seeds/seed.ts script that: creates 3 test users (admin@test.com, manager@test.com, user@test.com with password Test123!), creates 2 test projects, creates sample timesheets and entries. Run with: npm run seed. Test: execute seed, verify users/projects/timesheets in database.
acceptance_criteria: Seed script creates test users with correct roles
Can run multiple times (upsert or clear first)

intent: Create Dockerfile and docker-compose for backend
instructions: Create Dockerfile: FROM node:18, COPY package*.json, npm install, COPY src/, RUN npm run build, EXPOSE 3001, CMD npm run start:prod. Create docker-compose.yml with: backend service, postgres service (port 5432, volume), environment variables. Test: docker-compose up starts backend and postgres, health check passes.
acceptance_criteria: Backend connects to postgres in container

intent: Test auth flow: signup, login, JWT, role-based access
instructions: Test scenarios: signup new user (200, JWT returned), login with correct password (200, JWT), login with wrong password (401), access protected endpoint without JWT (401), with invalid JWT (401), with valid JWT (200). Test roles: create endpoint requiring MANAGER, test USER (403), MANAGER (200), ADMIN (200).
acceptance_criteria: Signup -> login -> dashboard access flow works

intent: Test 8hr/day and 40hr/week constraints at API level
instructions: Test: POST entry 8 hours (pass). POST 0.1 hours same day (fail, > 8). POST entries totaling 40 hours week (pass). POST 1 more hour (fail, > 40). Test with different days: 8 hrs Mon, 8 Tue, 8 Wed, 8 Thu, 8 Fri = 40 (pass). Add 1 more hour any day (fail). Test API validation (not just frontend).

intent: Test timesheet submit, approve, reject workflow
instructions: Test: user creates draft timesheet, tries to submit (no entries, fails). Adds entries, submits (status->pending). Tries to add entry (fails, pending is read-only). Manager approves (status->approved, read-only). Manager rejects (status->draft, shows comment). User edits and resubmits.

intent: Test report calculations and CSV export accuracy
instructions: Test: create 3 approved timesheets with known hours, generate report for date range, verify totals match calculation (spot-check). Export to CSV, verify file content matches report. Test date range filtering (include one week, exclude another). Test permission: user sees own, manager sees team.
